licensure.disciplinary_grounds.rationale: These nine buckets capture the dominant clusters across all states: fraudulent acts tied to obtaining or using a license; criminal convictions; incompetence/negligence/substandard work; violations of statutes, codes, or board rules; improper lending, transferring, or misusing a license; aiding or engaging in unlicensed practice; contract abandonment, fund diversion, and financial failures toward clients or suppliers; substance abuse and physical/mental impairment; and a residual bucket for administrative failures (continuing education, recordkeeping, child support, reporting obligations) that do not fit the primary clusters.

profession_specific.license_tiers.rationale: The items naturally cluster by career-ladder tier (apprentice → journeyman → master), business-entity license type (plumbing contractor vs. broader general/engineering contractor), scope-restricted licenses (specialty, limited, residential-only), add-on endorsements (medical gas, fire sprinkler, water supply protection), and the small residual group of inspectors and administrators, covering all rows without leaving a large uncategorized tail.
